item.title: Unification Church leader Hak Ja Han jailed for corruption
item.description: A South Korean court sentences an 83-year-old church leader to two years in prison for bribing the wife of ousted conservative president Yoon Suk Yeol as well as other corruption charges. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Dolly Parton laid to rest at private service as Dollyfest announced
item.description: The queen of country was interred next to her late husband in an intimate ceremony attended by close family Dolly Parton was laid to rest in a private ceremony in Nashville on Friday, her family has confirmed. The queen of country music, who died aged 80 on 25 August “after bravely facing a brief battle with cancer”, was interred at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum alongside her husband of 60 years, Carl Thomas. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - Culture. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Supreme Court lets construction continue on Trump's $558m ballroom
item.description: A divided Supreme Court has allowed the White House to continue construction on a $558 million ballroom project as lawsuits play out, a win for US President Donald Trump as he remakes the capital in his image. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Remote communities cut off as MinRes claims $158k from roads budget
item.description: A WA council will refund Chris Ellison's multi-billion-dollar mining company nearly $160,000 after the state government overturned a controversial Supreme Court case, with residents in isolated areas caught in the middle. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Kimberley Putland and Alistair Bates

item.title: Live: Oil prices surge on latest US-Iran flare-up, ASX to slip as housing slump continues
item.description: The latest flare-up in hostilities between the US and Iran have led to a 3 per cent surge in the oil price. The Australian share market is likely to start its day lower. House prices are falling in most of the nation's capital cities. Follow the day's events on the ABC News live markets blog. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Ziffer

item.title: Proposal for public walkway around waterside mansions survives vote
item.description: A proposal for a waterfront walkway around Hobart's historic Battery Point suburb has been debated for decades. The plan has lived to see another day, despite the local council's CEO recommending it be abandoned. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Sophie Jaggers

item.title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels since Nepal-Tibet floods
item.description: Rescuers are racing to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites since last week's catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll passes 950 with more than 4,400 people missing. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Live: Voters sent Labor message in WA by-election loss, Wong says
item.description: Acting Prime Minister Penny Wong acknowledges voters sent Labor a message in the recent WA state by-election won by One Nation. Follow live. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: New Sydney women's refuge thanks entirely to philanthropic donations
item.description: Mary's House Services in Sydney's north will open a second refuge for women and children thanks to philanthropic donations, after the charity failed to secure federal government funding. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Man shot dead in 'targeted' Sydney home invasion, police say
item.description: A man believed to be in his 20s has been shot dead during a home invasion south-west of Sydney, police say. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Fracked gas from Beetaloo Basin will flow to NT power grid from today
item.description: As of today, gas fracked from the Beetaloo Basin will flow into the Northern Territory's power grid, with the CLP forecasting the project will generate billions in economic value. But environmental activists say hundreds of Territorians oppose the project. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Matt Garrick and Kylie Stevenson

item.title: Farm-based nanopore sequencing study reports reliable genetic testing results
item.description: Fast, on-farm genetic testing for cattle is practical and achievable for northern producers, according to University of Queensland research. In partnership with Meat & Livestock Australia and the Department of Primary Industries, a team from UQ's Queensland Alliance for Agriculture and Food Innovation (QAAFI) tested low-pass nanopore sequencing on three commercial farms. Associate Professor Elizabeth Ross said the team produced reliable data for age, genomic breeding values (GBVs) and parentage for about 24 animals in less than 24 hours on each farm. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Former grand slam semifinalist smashes racquet after early US Open exit
item.description: Frenchwoman Lois Boisson has provided the first big blow-up of the US Open, smashing her racquet in disgust after going down in three sets to American 26th seed Emma Navarro. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Birrell saves match point as Aussies advance to US Open second rounds
item.description: Gritty Kim Birrell has overcome a match point and a restless night's sleep to break her first-round jinx with a maiden US Open victory in New York. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Politics of the parklands on show at Labor's big MotoGP reveal
item.description: The Malinauskas government's grand unveiling of its MotoGP track showed just how much pressure it faced over the environment. It's also opened up a fracture in the green movement. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Computers once threatened to take over jobs. Is history repeating with AI?
item.description: In 1968, Australians were warned that computers could wipe out entire professions. Now, a similar conversation is unfolding about artificial intelligence. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Concerns women will 'fall through the cracks' when mother-baby unit closes
item.description: While the mother-baby unit in Hobart deals with complex mental health challenges, staff have been told mothers must be "psychologically well" to be eligible for the service set to replace it. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Parents call for change as drug overdose deaths hit record high in Qld
item.description: Advocates say drug overdoses are "costing us people we shouldn't be losing" as unintentional drug-induced deaths surpass 2,000 for the first time. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Mother fears son will die before customised brain cancer vaccine trial
item.description: A world-first mRNA vaccine trial offers some hope to the family of a teenager dying from brain cancer, but they worry he will miss out on a place. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Netanyahu's rhetoric on settler violence doesn't match Israeli government action
item.description: If the Israeli prime minister sees settler violence as a "grave injustice", why can't one of the most powerful militaries in the world stop it from happening? The answer, as it often does, comes down to politics. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Man who hamstrung local council embroiled in years-long planning dispute
item.description: Luxury tourist villas being offered for hundreds of dollars a night were allegedly installed in a bushfire-prone area without prior permission, an ABC investigation has found. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Nepali survivors return to unrecognisable villages entombed in mud
item.description: The ABC sees firsthand villages buried under mud, locals sheltering in school halls with no running water and aid workers racing against time to stop disease spreading. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: New pressure on PM to allow telehealth for voluntary assisted dying
item.description: South Australia has become the first state to formally urge the Commonwealth to change a federal law preventing doctors from using telehealth in voluntary assisted dying (VAD). Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: First responders awarded decades after Australia's worst rail crash
item.description: First responders at the Granville rail disaster are being recognised with Australian Bravery Decorations, almost 50 years after the nation's worst train crash. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: 'Women just put up with it': Thousands suffer as prolapse surgery wait grows
item.description: Vaginal birth is the biggest risk factor for pelvic organ prolapse, but experts say women are not being told about the risks and warning signs signs prior to birth. It comes as wait lists for surgeries continue to grow. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: KPMG is losing million-dollar contracts, but hasn't hit the bottom yet
item.description: In the wake of scandals about the misuse of confidential information, embattled consulting firm KPMG is losing million-dollar contracts and cutting its workforce. And that's all before the corporate regulator, ASIC, has even opened its mouth. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Facial recognition technology 'scope creep' is upon us, experts warn
item.description: Industry groups say the move to facial scans in supermarkets is about safety, but analysts say that once the technology is installed, its "scope creep" paves the way for options like discriminatory pricing. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: China warns Pacific nations of 'consequences' for Taiwan forum invite
